The '''64th Golden Globe Awards''' honored the best in [[2006 in film|film]] and [[2006 in American television|American television of 2006]], as chosen by the [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] (HFPA). The ceremony was held on January 15, 2007, from the [[The Beverly Hilton|Beverly Hilton Hotel]] in [[Beverly Hills|Beverly Hills, California]] and were broadcast on [[NBC]] in the United States. Indicating the impact that animated films have had on the [[film industry]], the [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] announced in early 2006 that a Golden Globe would be awarded for the [[Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film|Best Animated Feature]] for the first time at this award ceremony.<ref>{{cite press release
 |publisher    = [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]]
 |date         = 2006-05-25
 |url          = http://www.goldenglobes.org/blog/2006/05/hfpa-announces-timetable-for64th-annual-golden-globe-awards/
 |title        = HFPA Announces Timetable for 64th Annual Golden Globe Awards
 |access-date   = 2006-06-13
 |archive-url  = https://archive.today/20130414205856/http://www.goldenglobes.org/blog/2006/05/hfpa-announces-timetable-for64th-annual-golden-globe-awards/
 |archive-date = 2013-04-14
 |url-status     = dead
}}</ref><ref>{{cite news
 | url = http://www.animationmagazine.net/events/golden-globes-in-toon-for-07/
 | first = Ryan
 | last = Ball
 | title = Golden Globes in Toon for ’07
 | publisher = Animation Magazine
 | date = 2006-01-30
 | access-date = 2006-06-13
 | archive-date = December 16, 2014
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141216164922/http://www.animationmagazine.net/events/golden-globes-in-toon-for-07/
 | url-status = live
 }}</ref>

''[[Dreamgirls (film)|Dreamgirls]]'' won the most awards, with 3 (including Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy). ''[[Babel (2006 film)|Babel]]'', received the most nominations, with 7 (only winning 1, for Best Motion Picture – Drama).

== Isaiah Washington press conference controversy ==
At a backstage press conference following the awards ceremony, [[Isaiah Washington]] addressed a media report involving alleged homophobic remarks towards ''[[Grey's Anatomy]]'' co-star [[T. R. Knight]], stating, "No, I did not call him a faggot." Knight's co-star, [[Katherine Heigl]] condemned Washington for his remarks at a Golden Globes afterparty.<ref name="kltvheigl">{{cite news |title=Heigl Upset With Co-Star's Comments |url=https://www.kltv.com/story/5949750/heigl-upset-with-co-stars-comments/ |access-date=28 June 2026 |work=KLTV |date=17 January 2007}}</ref> The resulting scandal led to Washington's exit from the show.<ref name="apwashington">{{cite news |last1=Andreeva |first1=Nellie |title=Washington discharged from ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/washington-discharged-greys-anatomy-138160/ |work=The Hollywood Reporter |agency=The Associated Press |date=8 June 2007}}</ref>
